summary: Opaque native module with credential-harvesting and host-fingerprinting capabilities auto-executed on require()
details: The package consists of a single 10 MB Linux x86_64 native module (tools.linux-x64-gnu.node) declared as the package `main`, so `require('new-native-tools-linux-x64-gnu')` executes its native module-init inside the caller's Node.js process. The tarball contains no source code, no author, repository, or homepage metadata, and only a two-line README. The version string (`3.1.42-origin-chrom-468-delete-windows-32-bit-changelog-fix-412-1785840430`) resembles internal build-pipeline artifact naming rather than a public release. Extracted strings from the binary reveal a statically-linked HTTP/TLS client (`ureq_proto::util`), process-execution and privilege primitives (`posix_spawnp`, `execvp`, `setuid`, `chroot`), host-fingerprinting calls (`gethostname`, `getifaddrs`, `/etc/lsb-release`, `/dev/disk/by-id/`, `network_adapters`), and credential-file language (`Found login for `, `failed to read: `). The combination of an opaque binary as the sole import-time payload, absent publisher identity, staging-artifact version metadata, and stealer-shaped capability strings (bundled network stack + credential file access + host reconnaissance + process spawn/privilege) is consistent with an install/import-time credential stealer or dropper rather than a legitimate native addon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
